channel.title: What NBA players and coaches have said about Puerto Rico | HoopsMatic
channel.description: The latest quotes about Puerto Rico from NBA players, coaches and executives, with context and sources.

item.title: Jose Alvarado on Puerto Rico, Bad Bunny
item.description:
Stefan Bondy:Jose Alvarado on Bad Bunny halftime show:

“Hell yeah. Can’t wait, you know. That’s a big opportunity for Puerto Ricans expanding. Especially me, being Boricua. But it’s big. For him to do what he did for us when he did the show (in Puerto Rico), it was tremendous. I went to the show, it was the best show I’ve ever been a part of. And he’s just doing a great job and I’m glad he’s able to show it at the highest level.”

Jose Alvarado on Puerto Rico, Bad Bunny, Feb 8, 2026. Source: Twitter.

item.title: Khaman Maluach on Puerto Rico
item.description:
“The Olympics now was the next level because now I’m playing Team USA, Serbia, Puerto Rico,”

Khaman Maluach on Puerto Rico, Jun 25, 2025. Source: Andscape.

item.title: Stephen Curry on LeBron James, Puerto Rico
item.description:
Stephen Curry:

“It’s positive self-talk. We were winning, and I was doing my part—setting screens, playing hard—but I wasn’t making shots. I knew at some point I’m going to need to make some shots because that’s why I’m here. After we played Puerto Rico, I was doing an interview, and they were asking me, 'What’s wrong with your shot? Are you worried about it?' I said, 'No, we’re winning, and I know a flurry is coming.' As soon as I said that, LeBron walks behind me and says, 'Damn right it is.' That gave me a lot of confidence. It caught me off guard because, you know, I had to get used to liking that guy after all of our battles. But it was a confidence boost, and it came at the right time.”

Stephen Curry on LeBron James, Puerto Rico, Sep 8, 2024. Source: YouTube.

item.title: Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico
item.description:
J.J. Barea:

“I think so. Maybe after this year’s over, I’ll see how I feel and maybe play another one in Puerto Rico. But it depends how I feel. But yeah, I think going overseas or other stuff like that, I think I’m done with that, but you never know. I think I’ll be done with that.”

Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico, May 21, 2021. Source: Dallas Morning News.

item.title: Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico
item.description:
J.J. Barea:

“Long story short, that same summer that I signed with the Mavericks, I played on that team. That team left for a while, and now it’s coming back with a new owner. The team is in San Juan, the capital, so it will be really good for Puerto Rican basketball and the pro league down there. It’s really important for the kids and the fans to have a league in Puerto Rico, so this year should be a lot of fun.”

Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico, May 21, 2021. Source: Dallas Morning News.

item.title: Channing Frye on Puerto Rico
item.description:
“I went to Puerto Rico with my kids and I saw our best friends who live down there and their kids are 12, 11, 10. My son is eight now. I'm like, ‘I want to go his practice and not have to worry about my practice.’ I want to make time for them. “What some of these young fellas don't understand is your whole life is on a selfish bubble, what's best for you, what you want to do. For me it took a while, but my dad instinct, and my husband and family guy kicked in. What can I do for my family? Money is awesome, but at this point I've had enough people either die or go away through relationships that couldn't get kept up. That's what's most important, making something outside of basketball.”

Channing Frye on Puerto Rico, Mar 3, 2019. Source: Cleveland Plain Dealer.

item.title: Adam Silver on Puerto Rico
item.description:
“And in Puerto Rico, it’s insane. People were praying for me every day. This never happened to me before. The support you get, it’s been crazy. And it’s special.”

Adam Silver on Puerto Rico, Feb 2, 2019. Source: mavs.com.

item.title: Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico
item.description:
J.J.Barea on Puerto Rico:

“It’s awful. People are struggling. … We need a lot of help. It’s going to take a while. It’s just starting.”

Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico, Sep 27, 2017. Source: Twitter @espn_macmahon.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico
item.description:
“I’ve started kind of a ‘YouCaring’ page…just trying to raise the funds to kind of bring Puerto Rico back and help Puerto Rico by any means necessary,”

Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico, Sep 26, 2017. Source: USA Today Sports.

item.title: Mark Cuban on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Cuban on Puerto Rico aid:

“I was really proud of J.J. and how quickly he got involved and how hard he worked to make all of this happen.”

Mark Cuban on Puerto Rico, Sep 26, 2017. Source: Twitter @espn_macmahon.

item.title: Maurice Baker on Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic
item.description:
“It’s a sacrifice league. The money is not that great, but it pays the bills. During the summer, I try to make that money up that I didn’t make playing in the D-League by playing in the Dominican Republic or Puerto Rico. It works for me,”

Maurice Baker on Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Jan 8, 2016. Source: Yahoo! Sports.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Anthony told ESPN in an interview.

“I just always kept it to myself and among my circle. Going to games, sneaking into games, and just watching and being around the sport over the years. The more time I start spending in Puerto Rico over the past six, seven years, I realized there was kind of a void down there on my island.”

Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico, Jun 12, 2015. Source: Wall Street Journal.

item.title: Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico
item.description:
A sampling of how the Mavs plan to spend their All-Star breaks: J.J. Barea:

“Puerto Ricoooooooooo!!! I got my son’s birthday in Puerto Rico. The beach and the pool. It should be a good weekend. My high school also has a big tournament that they named after me.”

Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico, Feb 13, 2015. Source: ESPN.com.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Carmelo Anthony on playing with Puerto Rico:

“Actually I considered playing with Puerto Rico back in 2004, but they told me that if I play with Puerto Rico I would never play for Team USA ever again.”

Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico, Jul 15, 2012. Source: HoopsHype.

item.title: Al Thornton on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Al Thornton:

“I was told if I play well here (in Puerto Rico), I would have chances to get back to the NBA. That was the reason why I came to play in this league.”

Al Thornton on Puerto Rico, Mar 11, 2012. Source: El Nuevo Dia.

item.title: Rashad McCants on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Rashad McCants:

“My agent advised me to play in the Puerto Rican League and considering how many NBA players have come to play this season, I think it was a good idea. Maybe if I play well here some NBA team will give me a legitimate chance to fight for a roster spot.”

Rashad McCants on Puerto Rico, Mar 8, 2012. Source: Primera Hora.

item.title: Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico
item.description:
JJ Barea:

“Oh she’s doing awesome. We’re expecting a little boy here soon, we’ve got a couple weeks and she’s been doing awesome. She’s here in Minnesota. She’s from Puerto Rico so we were in the same place, we were both single at the same time and I sent her a text and we kept it moving,”

Jose Juan Barea on Puerto Rico, Feb 5, 2012. Source: CBS Minnesota.

item.title: Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Carmelo Anthony:

“I wouldn't rule out playing in Puerto Rico. I keep that option open. I'd have to what offers are out there.”

Carmelo Anthony on Puerto Rico, Aug 6, 2011. Source: Primera Hora.

item.title: Udonis Haslem on Puerto Rico
item.description:
Haslem told Primera Hora.

“Carlos (Arroyo) talked to me about playing for the Puerto Rican National Team, but last year I was just focused in getting ready for the NBA season and I didn't want any distractions. But it's interesting. I don't know a lot about the whole process of playing with Puerto Rico, but I don't rule it out for the future.”

Udonis Haslem on Puerto Rico, Jun 7, 2011. Source: Primera Hora.

item.title: Rick Pitino on Puerto Rico
item.description:
“I was so looking forward to coaching the Puerto Rico national team, but too many conflicts arose,”

Rick Pitino on Puerto Rico, Apr 27, 2011. Source: Minneapolis Star-Tribune.

item.title: Phil Jackson on Puerto Rico
item.description:
He recalled interviewing for an assistant's job with Stan Albeck, who was the Bulls' coach before Collins.

“I was coaching in Puerto Rico and I came up with a Panama hat on and I had a beard, and Stan thought I was alittle kooky at that time,”

Phil Jackson on Puerto Rico, Jan 1, 2011. Source: Los Angeles Daily News.
